title: Cheaper to make, costlier to keep
units_note: All money figures in ₹ lakh unless marked. Costs are shown in brackets, e.g. (290).

brief.headline: Sales up 20%. Costs per unit down. And a ₹20L profit became a ₹20L loss.
brief.story: Boom Audio designs wireless earbuds in Noida and sells them on Amazon, Flipkart and its own website. July to September was its biggest quarter ever, and it even cut the cost of each unit by switching suppliers. Yet it swung to a loss. The customer service team says couriers are smashing parcels. The founder is about to switch logistics partners.

body.text: Average selling price held at about ₹500 per unit.
Return rate (refunds within 7 days): 6% in Q1, 7% in Q2. Refunds are already deducted from revenue.

causes.label: Couriers are damaging parcels in transit
causes.feedback: Damage claims against couriers held at 0.4%. "Damaged in transit" is just the support script's default reason.

causes.label: More customers are returning products for refunds
causes.feedback: Refund returns went from 6% to 7%, and refunds are already netted out of revenue. The cost that jumped is warranty replacements.

causes.label: Ad spend became inefficient
causes.feedback: Ads still return ₹10 of revenue per rupee.

causes.label: The rupee weakened and pushed up import costs
causes.feedback: Landed cost per unit fell, from ₹290 to ₹285.

causes.label: Cheaper battery cells from a new supplier are failing, driving warranty replacements

causes.label: Logistics costs went up
causes.feedback: Logistics rose ₹5L, in line with 20% more units.

causes.feedback: Cost of goods actually fell as a share of revenue.

bonus.question: Batches B-0712 and B-0715 shipped 48,000 units and have 11,760 claims so far. Claims usually arrive 30–90 days after sale, and 34% of the oldest B-0712 units (past 90 days) have claimed. What's the best estimate of claims still to come from these two batches?
options: About 4,500 more, roughly ₹23L of further replacement cost
bonus.explanation: If 34% of units eventually claim, the two batches will produce about 48,000 × 34% ≈ 16,300 claims. 11,760 have arrived, so about 4,500 more are coming, at ₹500 each ≈ ₹23L. The founder should set that money aside now and recall or pre-emptively replace units still in stock.

explanation.answer: In July Boom switched to cheaper battery cells from VoltCell. Two batches built with them (48,000 units) are failing: 11,760 warranty claims, with the lab finding swollen or dead batteries. Warranty replacement costs jumped from ₹10L to ₹66L. That ₹56L jump is more than the whole ₹40L fall in profit; growth elsewhere covered the rest. The ₹21 saved per cell is costing ₹500 per claim.
fastest_path: Open the P&L. Warranty replacements jumped from ₹10L to ₹66L; everything else moved with sales.
Open the warranty claims log. Claims jumped to 13,200, mostly from batches B-0712 and B-0715, arriving 30–90 days after purchase.
Open the repair centre lab report. 81% of tested units have battery failures, 92% of them from those two batches.
Open the supplier & batch register. Those are exactly the batches built with VoltCell's cheaper cells.
traps: The returns report is the misleading file: "damaged in transit" is the support script's default, and courier damage claims never moved.
Customer service believes it's couriers, and the founder is about to change logistics partners. That would fix nothing.
"A design flaw in the new model" is the near-miss: every model fails, but only in the VoltCell batches.
explanation.lesson: A cheaper part is only cheaper until it fails in the customer's hand.
